confirmed_facts.text: OpenShell is the safe, private runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: OpenShell is the safe, private runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents.

confirmed_facts.text: Agents are most useful when they can read files, install packages, call APIs, and use credentials.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: Agents are most useful when they can read files, install packages, call APIs, and use credentials.

confirmed_facts.text: OpenShell gives them that capability without giving them unrestricted access to your data, secrets, or network.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: OpenShell gives them that capability without giving them unrestricted access to your data, secrets, or network.

confirmed_facts.text: You declare what each agent can touch in a policy, and OpenShell enforces it.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: You declare what each agent can touch in a policy, and OpenShell enforces it.

confirmed_facts.text: OpenShell governs what agents can do in two ways: it instruments the kernel to enforce policy on every file access, system call, and network connection at runtime, and it uses formal verification to check what a policy change would allow before it is applied.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: OpenShell governs what agents can do in two ways: it instruments the kernel to enforce policy on every file access, system call, and network connection at runtime, and it uses formal verification to check what a policy change would allow before it is applied.

confirmed_facts.text: Kernel controls confine which files it can access and which system calls it can make, and every network connection passes through a policy check before it leaves the sandbox.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: Kernel controls confine which files it can access and which system calls it can make, and every network connection passes through a policy check before it leaves the sandbox.
